resolvedFindings: The prior exact-head review found that Android did not prove the unit-wide no-auto-resume policy. The player now converts transient audio-focus suppression into an explicit pause, and the focal test verifies it remains paused after focus is returned.

The prior exact-head review found cleanup could leave its WAV. Fixture creation now occurs inside the protected scope; stop, activity finish and deletion are attempted independently, and the test asserts both successful stop and absence of the file.
review.scopeLimit: Platform focal coverage proves safe pausing for focus, route, interruption and foreground loss. Physical Bluetooth/wired routing, microphone permission, prolonged background playback and audio outside Chat remain outside this unit.

notes: The Android focal test launches the real app, plays a generated local WAV through the production Media3 service, obtains focus, then verifies that a competing foreground focus request pauses before end-of-media.

The Web focal test executes the production Kotlin/Wasm bridge in Chrome Headless and verifies a hidden-document visibility event pauses the active player and cleanup removes the registry/listener ownership.
The iOS focal suite executes the production AVPlayer engine on an x86_64 iOS 26.5 simulator and covers interruption start/end, old-route unavailability and app resignation.
The iOS execution remains bound to identical production and test Git blobs after Android and Web test-only additions; it was not repeated solely for the amended Product SHA.
This unit adopts pause-without-auto-resume as the safe lifecycle policy. It does not claim prolonged background playback or physical-device routing.
